- **Items or steps:** 6 mistakes, no count said at the start. Items run 1:18 to 2:15: wrong terminal (0:15-1:33, 1:18), strip length (1:33-3:48, 2:15, the longest because it has two sides, too much and too little, plus the strip-gauge check), hook direction (3:48-5:44, 1:56), push-in holes (6:04-7:58, 1:54), two wires under one screw (7:58-9:28, 1:30), the screwdriver bit (9:28-11:31, 2:03, close behind because it compares three bits and shows two). Order: the order of the job (which screw, how much to strip, which way to hook), then the two shortcuts people take (push-in, doubling up), then the tool that makes every joint tighter. The stakes rise across the middle (polarity, then fire from a loose joint, then code and fire), and it ends on the lowest-stakes, most useful item.
- **Promise devices:** a "you might be surprised how many people don't know" flag on item 1 (0:20, problem you didn't know); a spot-the-mistake question (4:03) the next lines answer; a check at home (3:14, the strip gauge); the item openers as priority flags ("this is a big one", 8:01). No numbered count and no step count: the title's "biggest mistakes" is the only promise.
- **Forward lines:** 6, one per item ("so for this next mistake" and variants, plus "that leads me to the next mistake" at 3:48). Longest gap between a forward line or payoff: about 2:15 (inside item 2, 1:33-3:48), held by the too-much and too-little demonstrations.
- **Stakes:** strong and frequent. First at 1:02 ("so dangerous", then short circuit, shock or fire at 1:11); fire returns in item 2 (2:26), as arcing and heating in item 4 (7:33), and in item 5 (8:51, "incredibly dangerous", against code). About 6 danger lines in 12 minutes, each tied to a specific mechanism, so it stays in proportion, but it never says power off.
- **Safety lines:** none. No breaker-off, no verify-dead, no call-an-electrician line anywhere (a recent comment notes the absence). All the work is on loose devices on the bench.
- **CTA placement:** mid-video at 5:44-6:04 (about 20 seconds, 84 words: thumbs up or a comment, framed as helping the video reach others), between items 3 and 4 at 48%; at the end, 11:31-11:59: tool links in the description, playlists, thumbs up, questions in the comments.
- **Ending:** the last item ends on a side-by-side tool demonstration, then links, playlists, a hope it helped, a like ask and an open comment ask. No recap.
- **What sets it apart from other models of its type:**

(371 likes); and "Do you realize how rare it is to post a diy video and not get a bunch of 'experts' to rip you a new one? Well, this guy pulled it off." (600 likes). The strip gauge is the single most-thanked tip: "3:15 strip gauge measurement on the back to know exactly how much wire to strip. Truly a gem tip!!!!" (166 likes). The most-liked viewer comment is a memory aid for the screw colours (1K likes), which shows how item 1 is retold. The opening takes 15 seconds and names no count; each item then follows the same order (the mistake shown, why it fails, what can happen, the right way) at about 210 words a minute. Viewers say they're using it to redo whole houses ("I'm in the middle of replacing all of my receptacles in my 1987 home. This video helps a lot.", 58 likes), and one suggests the step it leaves out: checking polarity on the circuit before changing anything (84 likes).
